summary: Tenant optimization safe-exit: create tenant snapshot and emergency toggle for aggressive prefetch + int8 profile
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightWell Health reports a sudden increase in 95/99p tail latency and sporadic stream disconnects after applying an optimization bundle (kv-prefetch enabled + int8 quantization profile) to their dedicated tenant. They request assistance to create a per-tenant safe snapshot (config + runtime state) and a minimal emergency toggle to disable only the aggressive prefetched KV path while preserving other optimizations.

Impact:
- Elevated 95p/99p latency from ~120ms to 900-1,200ms for chat/streaming flows.
- ~3% of streaming sessions terminating with a handshake error in the last 12 hours.
- Business impact: BrightWell deferred next-week rollout until mitigated. Dedicated tenant — high priority.

Timeline / Context:
- 2026-03-09 14:10 UTC: Customer applied optimizer bundle via Console (profile: bw-health-int8-prefetch-v2).
- 2026-03-09 17:05 UTC: Support observed first latency alerts on per-tenant dashboard.
- 2026-03-10 09:30 UTC: Customer opened support chat and asked for safe rollback guidance.

Environment:
- Tenant ID: tenant_bw_9812 (provided to Support privately).
- Deployment: Dedicated GPU pool (p3-equivalent nodes), runtime v3.8.1, autoscaler enabled.

Steps to reproduce (best-effort):
1) Create a request against the customer's tenant using the same headers and seq lengths:
   - curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
     -H "Authorization: Bearer <t.tenant_bw_9812>"
     -d '{"model":"meta-llama-2-13b","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a patient medical assistant."}, {"role":"user","content":"Generate a 1,200-token discharge summary with medication list and warnings."}], "stream": true }'
2) Observe increased token latency on 2nd+ chunk and occasional stream disconnects at ~token 512-1024.

Observed behavior:
- 95/99p per-token latency spikes and a correlated increase in ephemeral 5xx-like stream handshake errors.
- Heap of logs shows repeated KV cache eviction/rehydration for the tenant.
- Kernel-level quantization paths show occasional dequantization fallback for longer sequences.

Expected behavior:
- Stable 95p latency within SLA (<=250ms) and no additional stream disconnects after optimization.

Attachments / links:
- Per-tenant dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/tenants/tenant_bw_9812/metrics (customer-shared view)
- Alert graph (99p latency): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/latency/tenant_bw_9812
- Support Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01SUPP123/p1678504800000000

Request from customer:
1) Create a point-in-time snapshot of this tenant's optimizer config + runtime metadata (flags, KV mapping, current cache keys) that Support/SRE can use to fully restore the exact pre-change state if needed.
2) Provide a minimal, tenant-scoped toggle/script to disable the aggressive KV-prefetch path and switch quantization profile to the previous int8->fp16 fallback for live traffic with minimal disruption (preferably without tenant-wide model pin changes).
3) Verification checklist and recommended smoke tests for the customer to validate before full rollback.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:02 UTC - Asha Mehta (Support): Initial triage done; collected tenant ID and recent console audit. Asked engineering to confirm snapshot feasibility for dedicated tenants.

2026-03-10 12:45 UTC - SRE Channel (#sre-support): Liam O'Connor assigned for tenant snapshot. Noted that runtime v3.8.1 supports per-tenant config snapshots via 'rwctl tenant snapshot' but must coordinate with autoscaler to quiesce nodes for consistent KV map.

2026-03-10 15:20 UTC - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Performed dry-run snapshot on staging cluster; created command sequence and checklist. Shared tentative rollback toggle: 'tenant.config.optimizer.prefetch=false' and 'tenant.config.quant.profile_override=fp16-fallback'. Need windows to apply in prod with very small traffic split.

2026-03-11 08:30 UTC - BrightWell Health (Customer): Requested that snapshot include the exact keyset for KV cache (for auditing) and that rollback be reversible within 15 minutes if negative impact observed.

2026-03-11 11:00 UTC - Asha Mehta (Support): Confirmed reversible plan and proposed a blue/green traffic split at 5% for 10 minutes for verification before full switch. Created SUP-63722 as follow-up for automated gate script (linked).
investigation_notes: Heap traces indicate increased cache churn for this tenant post-prefetch enabling; eviction rate up 4.6x compared to baseline.
Kernel logs show occasional fallback to FP16 decode on sequences > 1024 tokens which increases CPU scheduling and blocks token emission path.
Autoscaler metrics show transient pod restarts correlated with heavy KV rehydration; possible interplay between continuous batching and prefetch causing hot-shard pressure.

Staging dry-run snapshot succeeded using 'rwctl tenant snapshot create --tenant tenant_bw_9812 --include-kv-keys --out /snapshots/tenant_bw_9812-2026-03-10.tar.gz' (requires maintenance window for consistent KV capture in prod).
workaround: Applied a recommended emergency canary: tenant.config.optimizer.prefetch=false for 5% of traffic via traffic-split (blue group). Provided rollback command to customer. If canary shows latency improvement, escalate to 25% then 100% with 10m observation windows. Manual snapshot saved at s3://redwood-tenant-snapshots/tenant_bw_9812/2026-03-10.tar.gz
next_steps: 1) Schedule 20-minute maintenance window with BrightWell operations for full prod snapshot. 2) Run canary toggle script and monitor 95/99p latency and stream error rate for selected cohort. 3) If canary improves metrics, apply tenant-level toggle to full traffic, then plan safe re-enablement of prefetch with lower concurrency thresholds and updated cache limits. 4) Post-mortem and runbook update to include tenant snapshot run flow.
resolution: WIP - canary deployed to 5% traffic (2026-03-11 14:00 UTC). Early signal: 95p latency reduced ~40% for canary cohort after 8 minutes. Monitoring ongoing. No full rollback executed yet.
public_notes_for_customer: We have created a point-in-time snapshot and started a controlled canary disabling the aggressive prefetch for a small fraction of your traffic. Support will monitor and share minute-by-minute metrics during the verification window. If you prefer, we can proceed with a full toggle immediately; otherwise we will expand the canary on successful verification.
suggested_smoke_tests: Submit a 1,200-token streaming chat request (same as reproduction) and confirm continuous token emission with no disconnects.
Measure 95p/99p per-token latency for 10 repeated runs and compare to pre-change baseline.
Run a short burst load (50 concurrent streams) to verify no spikes in KV evictions or pod restarts.
